security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU TCG, when a conditional branch is not-taken and gen_branch() records a CTR entry where ctrtarget != PC of the next sequential instruction (e.g., if ctx->cur_insn_len is incorrectly computed for compressed/RVC instructions, or a future code change inadvertently uses the branch offset instead of fall-through PC as dest for the non-taken path), the ctrtarget CSR field no longer reflects the actual fall-through target.
security_spec.summary: ctrtarget for not-taken branches must hold next-sequential-PC; QEMU TCG must ensure dest=pc+cur_insn_len in the not-taken gen_branch path at trans_rvi.c.inc:295 else guest CFI monitoring reads wrong target

findings.finding: Non-taken branch CTR dest correctly computed as fall-through PC via gen_pc_plus_diff(dest, ctx, ctx->cur_insn_len). ctx->cur_insn_len is set by insn_len() (returning 2 for RVC, 4 otherwise), so the fall-through address is always pc_next + correct_insn_len. The ctx->pc_save save/restore at lines 274/301 ensures the TCG relative-offset math is consistent.
Taken branch CTR dest correctly computed as branch target via gen_pc_plus_diff(dest, ctx, a->imm). The imm field is the signed branch offset decoded by the instruction decoder.

ctr_dst stored with CTRTARGET_MISP (bit 0) explicitly cleared: dst & ~CTRTARGET_MISP. This is correct per the spec — the MISP bit is set/cleared separately by CPU prediction logic, not by the recording path.

CTRDATA_TYPE_NONTAKEN_BRANCH filter inversion correctly implemented: the NONTAKEN_BRANCH control bit is an enable bit (not an inhibit bit), so the check uses inverted logic: skip only when the bit is NOT set. This matches the RISC-V CTR spec where bit 4 of xctrctl enables non-taken branch recording.

gen_pc_plus_diff correctly computes the absolute destination as ctx->base.pc_next + diff. In the non-taken CTR path, diff=ctx->cur_insn_len, yielding pc_next+cur_insn_len = fall-through PC. For PCREL mode, the relative offset is computed as dest - ctx->pc_save, where pc_save is the current PC at translation time (not -1, which is asserted).

insn_len correctly decodes RISC-V instruction length: if low 2 bits == 3 (non-compressed), length=4; otherwise length=2 (compressed/RVC). This ensures ctx->cur_insn_len is 2 for RVC branch instructions (c.beqz, c.bnez) and 4 for standard branches.

CSR indirect access to ctrtarget correctly maps logical entry numbers to circular buffer indices. Entry >= depth returns read-as-zero. The wr_mask parameter (from sireg2 indirect access) controls which bits are writable; no additional hardware writability mask is needed here beyond wr_mask.
CSR write to ctrdata correctly applies CTRDATA_MASK (type + CCV + CCM + CCE fields) on top of wr_mask, preventing writes to reserved bits in the data entry.

All CTR state is migrated: mctrctl, sctrdepth, sctrstatus, vsctrctl, and all three arrays (ctr_src, ctr_dst, ctr_data) at maximum depth (256 entries). Migration is conditional on ext_smctr or ext_ssctr being enabled.

findings.finding: riscv_cpu_reset_hold does not explicitly reset any CTR-related state (mctrctl, sctrdepth, sctrstatus, vsctrctl, ctr_src/dst/data arrays). While QOM object_initialize zero-initializes CPU state on cold boot, a warm reset path could leave stale CTR entries in arrays and stale WRPTR/depth values. Since mctrctl defaults to 0 (recording disabled), the stale data is not directly accessible until software configures mctrctl, but residual WRPTR/depth values could produce unexpected behavior if CTR recording is enabled post-reset without sctrdepth re-initialization.
